heroLead: Frisco City sits in southern Monroe County, timber country where the pulp and paper industry has shaped the local economy at least as much as oil and gas ever has, though mineral reservations from earlier decades still turn up regularly in deed records.
intro: If you are a Frisco City landowner or heir who came across a mineral reservation while reviewing a deed, or someone who has been quietly receiving a small royalty check without knowing much about where it comes from, we can help you understand the full picture.

sections.heading: Timberland deeds and buried mineral reservations
paragraphs: A lot of land around Frisco City passed through large timber companies at some point in the twentieth century, and it was common practice for those companies, or the families who sold to them, to reserve mineral rights even while selling the surface and timber outright. Decades later, those reservations are often still technically valid, sitting quietly in the chain of title until someone, an heir, a new owner doing a title search, notices them.
If that describes your situation, we can trace the reservation back to confirm exactly who holds it today.

sections.heading: What we look for before quoting
paragraphs: Current or historical lease activity, proximity to any producing wells in Monroe County, and a clear chain of title connecting the reservation to you. Interests with an active royalty history are the most straightforward to value; undeveloped reservations require more judgment and a more conservative, honestly explained number.
We walk you through exactly which category your Frisco City interest falls into before any offer is made.

faqs.question: I found a mineral reservation from an old timber company deed. Do I own it?
faqs.answer: Possibly, if the reservation passed to you through inheritance or a prior purchase; we can trace the chain of title to confirm current ownership.

faqs.question: Has there been any real oil and gas activity near Frisco City?
faqs.answer: Monroe County has seen periodic leasing and some production tied to the broader south Alabama Smackover trend, though it varies significantly by specific tract.

faqs.question: What if the reservation was never leased at all?
faqs.answer: We can still evaluate it, priced conservatively to reflect its undeveloped, speculative status rather than an active production history.

faqs.question: How long does title research usually take for a Frisco City interest?
faqs.answer: Often one to two weeks, depending on how far back we need to trace the chain of title and whether probate records are involved.
